info.title: Leap Incentives — Lookups
info.description:
Check which rebate programs a customer qualifies for, and keep that answer current as their situation changes. Three operations share one request shape:

  * `POST /beta/incentives/lookups` is the first call for a customer. It stores the customer and their devices, resolves the serving utility from the address, and evaluates eligibility.
  * `POST /beta/incentives/refreshes` re-evaluates a customer you have already looked up, against their stored address and devices. Send it to pick up newly launched programs and updated amounts, or to add, update, or remove individual devices.
  * `POST /beta/incentives/overrides` rebuilds an existing customer from a fresh request body: it re-resolves the address and serving utility, replaces the device set, and clears the customer attributes you previously supplied. Use it to correct a customer record before any application is submitted.

Authenticate every call with your Leap API key as a bearer token. Your account is identified by that key, so the customers, devices, and applications you read and write are always your own.

post.description: Check which rebate programs a customer qualifies for. Send the customer's address, classification, and devices; Leap returns the total incentive amount, a per-program breakdown, and a Connect URL the customer can use to apply.

200.description: Eligibility resolved (programs may be empty if the customer matches no candidates).

post.description: Re-run eligibility for a customer you've already looked up, using their stored address and devices — no need to resend them. Use this to pick up newly launched programs or updated incentive amounts.

200.description: Eligibility re-evaluated using the customer's stored state.

post.description: Replace an existing customer's device list, then re-run eligibility. Use this when a customer's equipment has changed. The previous device set is discarded.

200.description: Customer rebuilt from the request and eligibility re-evaluated.

PaymentRequired.description: `PLAN_REQUIRED`: the request set `create_application: true` and the partner is not on the Business plan. Lookups are free on every plan; creating applications needs the Business plan with a subscription that is `active`, `trialing` or `past_due`. Nothing was written: no customer, device or application row changed. `details[0].upgrade_url` links to the portal billing page. Retry with `create_application: false` to get eligibility without applications.

error.message: Creating applications requires a Business plan.

details.reason: create_application is true and the partner is not on the Business plan with an active, trialing or past_due subscription

Forbidden.description: You do not have permission to perform this operation

NotFound.description: Address is not covered by any utility we have territory data for. This is a coverage gap, not an internal failure — the caller should not retry.

Conflict.description:
The request cannot be applied without destroying a record the caller did not name, or one that no longer belongs to us alone. Both cases are raised by `/incentives/overrides`, and in both **nothing is modified on either side**.

  * `ADDRESS_OWNED_BY_ANOTHER_CUSTOMER` — the submitted `address`
    already belongs to a DIFFERENT customer of the same partner.
    Leap holds one customer per address per partner, so applying the override would have to merge or clobber the other record. Resolve the duplicate partner-side (or
    override the customer that already owns the address) and retry.
  * `CONNECT_APPLICATIONS_IN_FLIGHT` — the customer has at least one
    application that has already been started: any status other than
    `not_started`, including `rejected`, `declined` and `dismissed`. An override is
    a pre-submission correction; a filed claim has an external record
    and customer-uploaded documents behind it, so it is refused rather
    than discarded. The `reason` names the blocking application ids and
    their statuses. Resolve them first, or use a fresh `reference_id`
    for the corrected customer.
  * `CONNECT_CUSTOMER_SHARED`, `CONNECT_REFERENCE_ID_TAKEN` and
    `CONNECT_RESET_REFUSED` are reserved. They came from the Supabase
    permission check, which this API no longer calls, so none is
    returned today.

UnprocessableEntity.description: Request was syntactically valid but could not be processed (e.g., unknown device id, address could not be geocoded)

RateLimited.description: The shared per-partner rate limit for /incentives endpoints was exceeded (`error_code: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`). Back off and retry after the number of seconds indicated by the `Retry-After` header.

BadGateway.description:
An upstream dependency did not answer.

  * `GEOCODING_RATE_LIMITED` / `GEOCODING_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — the
    geocoder is unavailable or rate-limited.
  * `CONNECT_RESET_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONNECT_RESET_FAILED`,
    `CONNECT_MERGE_FAILED`, `CONNECT_MERGE_REJECTED`,
    `CONNECT_RESET_REJECTED`, `CONNECT_RESET_REFUSED_AFTER_REBUILD` and
    `CONNECT_REFERENCE_ID_TAKEN_AFTER_REBUILD` (`/overrides` only) are
    reserved. They reported the Supabase Connect reset, which this API no
    longer calls, so none is returned today.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Safe to surface to partners; no internal identifiers.

upgrade_url.description: Present on `PLAN_REQUIRED` only. The portal page where the partner chooses a paid plan.

reference_id.description: Your stable identifier for this customer. Leap uses it to recognise a returning customer, and you'll send it again on **Refresh incentives**, **Override incentives**, and when searching applications. It's scoped to you — another partner using the same value is a different customer.

customer_devices.description:
One entry per installation, at least one and at most 50. Each names a catalog `device_id` and an optional `partner_device_reference` that tells two installations of the same device apart. The inline `details` object carries per-installation attributes, for example `customer_device.purchase_price` or `customer_device.installation_date`.

On **Override incentives** this list replaces the customer's device set: every installation on file is discarded first, so their `customer_device_id`s are regenerated.

eiaid.description: Optional utility override. Supply it when you already know the customer's serving utility and the address-based match is unavailable or ambiguous: Leap uses this EIA utility id to select candidate programs instead of resolving the utility from the address. On this path the address isn't geocoded, so the response omits the `geocoding` block and any stored coordinates are left as they are. A value matching no utility fails the same way an unserved address does (404 `NO_UTILITY_AT_ADDRESS`).

supplier_eiaid.description:
Optional. The retail supplier the customer chose, such as a Texas retail electric provider or a CCA, by its EIA id. It must name a supplier record, or the request fails with 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`. The supplier's programs join the candidates, and it is returned in `utilities.suppliers` with `source: declared`. It never replaces the delivery utility in `eiaid`.

A declared supplier is stored on the customer. On `/lookups` a request without `supplier_eiaid` keeps the stored one, and `POST /incentives/refreshes` replays it. `/overrides` is a clean slate: it stores this request's value, and no value clears it.

A declared supplier replaces every supplier found by territory, so a customer on the edge of a CCA polygon who declares a different supplier gets only the declared supplier's programs. A CCA needs no declaration: without one it is resolved from its territory.

customer_details.description:
Customer attributes you're supplying, keyed by field name, for example `{"customer.utility_account_number": "0123456789"}`. Values are always strings. Facts about one installation go in that entry's `details` object instead.

Send project costs here, once per customer. `customer.installation_cost` is the services total for the whole job, before tax: labor, materials, and permits. `customer.total_project_cost` is the deal total including tax. Each device's equipment price goes in that device's `details` as `customer_device.purchase_price`.

In cost-based amounts, `customer.installation_cost` replaces each device's installation cost and the regional estimate. In installation cost checks, it stands in for the device's `customer_device.installation_cost`. Each cost calculation counts it once, and each program and each tier is its own calculation. Leap doesn't split it between devices or programs. It stays on file until you clear it. Send it as an empty string on a refresh, or leave it out of an override body.

Leap ignores a value that is negative, above 1,000,000,000, or written with more than six decimal places. Device-level costs apply instead. Text that isn't a number returns 400. A zero is a real zero. No calculation reads `customer.total_project_cost` yet.

An unrecognised key returns 400 and no incentives. The [Requirements reference](/setup-data-preferences) lists every key and its value form.

Omit or leave empty if you have none. Maximum 100 entries.

create_application.description: Create the Connect application records for this lookup's eligible programs, so the returned `connect_url` is a link the customer can open. Provisioning runs in the background and is normally in place within seconds. Defaults to `false`: lookup-only integrations are unaffected and no applications are created for them. Setting it to `true` needs the Business plan. On any other plan the request returns 402 `PLAN_REQUIRED` and writes nothing.

include_preview.description: Include your own unpublished partner offer in the results so you can test it before publishing. Only your own offer is ever included. Utility, state, and market programs are unaffected. Defaults to `false`.

reference_id.description: Partner's stable identifier for the customer. Must match an existing customer scoped to the authenticated `partner_id`; unknown reference IDs return 404.

customer_details.description:
Customer attributes to merge before re-evaluating, keyed by field name. Values are always strings. A key you send replaces what's on file, and a key you leave out is untouched. Use this to fill in facts as you learn them, rather than repeating a lookup.

Send project costs here, once per customer. `customer.installation_cost` is the services total for the whole job, before tax: labor, materials, and permits. `customer.total_project_cost` is the deal total including tax. Each device's equipment price goes in that device's `details` as `customer_device.purchase_price`.

In cost-based amounts, `customer.installation_cost` replaces each device's installation cost and the regional estimate. In installation cost checks, it stands in for the device's `customer_device.installation_cost`. Each cost calculation counts it once, and each program and each tier is its own calculation. Leap doesn't split it between devices or programs. It stays on file until you clear it. Send it as an empty string on a refresh, or leave it out of an override body.

Leap ignores a value that is negative, above 1,000,000,000, or written with more than six decimal places. Device-level costs apply instead. Text that isn't a number returns 400. A zero is a real zero. No calculation reads `customer.total_project_cost` yet.

An unrecognised key returns 400 and no incentives. The [Requirements reference](/setup-data-preferences) lists every key and its value form.

Omit or leave empty for no attribute changes. Maximum 100 entries.

customer_devices.description: Optional device merge set. An entry carrying a `customer_device_id` updates that installation in place; an entry without one adds a new installation. Installations already on file that you don't list are left untouched — sending a subset never deletes the rest.

remove_customer_device_ids.description: Remove installations by `customer_device_id`. Ids that don't match a device on this customer are ignored, so retries are safe.

remove_device_references.description: Remove installations by `partner_device_reference`. Every installation with a matching reference is removed; unknown references are ignored.

eiaid.description: Optional utility override, matching the one on **Look up incentives**. Supply an EIA utility id to re-resolve the customer's serving utility instead of reusing the one on file. Leap re-selects candidate programs against it, re-runs eligibility, and keeps the override for later calls on this customer.

supplier_eiaid.description: Optional. The retail supplier the customer chose, by its EIA id, with the same rules as `supplier_eiaid` on `/lookups`: it must name a supplier record (400 `INVALID_REQUEST` otherwise), it replaces any supplier found by territory, and it is stored on the customer. When omitted, the refresh uses the supplier stored by an earlier `/lookups`, `/overrides` or `/refreshes`, if any.

create_application.description: Create the Connect application records for this refresh's eligible programs, so the returned `connect_url` is a link the customer can open. It matches the flag on **Look up incentives** and defaults to `false`. Only a refresh that changes something has anything to create: one that supplies `customer_devices`, `customer_details` or a removal. A bare re-evaluation creates nothing, flag or no flag. Like a lookup, `true` needs the Business plan and returns 402 `PLAN_REQUIRED` on any other plan.

CustomerDeviceRef.description: One installation. New installations name their catalog device with `device_id`. On **Refresh incentives**, `customer_device_id` instead targets an installation already on file, for an in-place update.

device_id.description: The catalog device's `id`, from **Search device catalog** or the portal's Device profile mapping. Required on a new installation. Optional when `customer_device_id` targets an installation already on file, and must match that installation's catalog device when you do send it. A `device_id` that is not in the catalog is rejected with 422 `INVALID_DEVICE_ID`.

customer_device_id.description: Identifies one installation — this customer, this catalog device, your device reference. Leap assigns it on the first lookup and echoes it back in `customer_devices[]`; it is stable across later lookups and refreshes, and is regenerated only by **Override incentives**, which replaces the device set. Send it on **Refresh incentives** to update that installation in place; it is rejected with 400 on lookups and overrides.

partner_device_reference.description:
Partner-supplied per-installation identifier. Unique within the request. Echoed back in the response so partners can join their local records to the upserted `customer_device`.
Supplying it makes it the installation's identity: the entry addresses the stored installation holding that reference for that `device_id`, and nothing else.
Omitting it is supported and stable. The server matches the entry against the installations already on file for the customer by `device_id`, so reordering the array or sending a subset resolves to the same installations as before. It assigns `"1"`, `"2"`, ... (skipping any value already in use) only when it actually creates a new installation. Two entries for the same `device_id` with no reference are only accepted when the customer has no installation of that device yet; otherwise nothing but array position tells them apart, and the request is rejected with 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` asking for an explicit reference.

details.description:
Attributes for this one installation, keyed by field name, for example `{"customer_device.purchase_price": "699.00"}`. Values are always strings. Facts about the customer go in the request's `customer_details` object instead.

Send the equipment price here as `customer_device.purchase_price`. If you hold one services total for the whole job, send it once as `customer.installation_cost` in `customer_details`. Don't repeat it here, because a repeated total counts once per device. In cost-based amounts, the customer-level value replaces this device's installation cost and the regional estimate. Each cost calculation counts it once, not once per device. In installation cost checks, it stands in for this device's `customer_device.installation_cost`.

An unrecognised key returns 400 and no incentives. The [Requirements reference](/setup-data-preferences) lists every key and its value form.

Maximum 50 entries.

device_id.description: The catalog `device.id` resolved for this installation.

partner_device_reference.description: Server-resolved value (echoed verbatim if the partner supplied one; assigned `"1"`, `"2"`, ... otherwise).

customer_device_id.description: Leap's identifier for this installation. Store it — it's how you address that specific device on later calls.

address_line_1.description: Street address — house number and street name. Optional: omit it (or send null or an empty string, which are treated the same) to geocode on the ZIP alone. Whatever you send is echoed back verbatim in `geocoding.formatted_address`.

address_line_2.description: Optional secondary address line, such as an apartment, suite, or unit number.

city.description: City name. Optional: omit it (or send null or an empty string, which are treated the same) to geocode on the ZIP alone.

state.description: Two-letter US state abbreviation. Optional: omit it (or send null or an empty string, which are treated the same) to geocode on the ZIP alone. When you omit it, the server fills it from the geocoder's structured result and uses that value everywhere it would have used yours, including Partner Offer state gating, so an offer restricted to a list of states still matches a ZIP-only request. A value you send always wins over the derived one, and the response echoes your address as you sent it.

zip_code.description: US ZIP code, 5-digit or ZIP+4. Required on every request, and the only address field that is. A blank or malformed value is rejected with 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`.

country_code.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code. Defaults to `US`.

reference_id.description: Echoes the `reference_id` from the request — the partner's stable identifier for this customer.

customer_devices.description: Per-installation echo. One entry per request entry, with the resolved (server-filled if absent) `partner_device_reference` and the upserted `customer_device.id`.

connect_url.description: Deep link to hand the customer so they can apply: `https://connect.incentives.leap.energy/{company}/refId/{reference_id}`, where `{company}` is your registration nickname. **Omitted entirely when the lookup surfaces no eligible incentive** — there is nothing to apply for, so check that the field is present before showing a link. Also omitted on every plan except Business.

program_details.description: One entry per eligible (or conditionally eligible) program. Empty when no candidate programs match the (utility, customer_classification, device_category) filter.

devices_ignored.description:
`/incentives/lookups` only. Entries the request named that were NOT written, because the request resolved to a customer that already exists and the entry named an installation that customer does not have. Absent or empty on every other outcome, and always absent for a customer created by this request.
`/incentives/lookups` establishes a customer's device set. Adding to one that already exists is what `/incentives/refreshes` does — send the new installation there. The call still returns 200 and still evaluates the entries that WERE recognised, so a partner-side mistake never fails an otherwise-answerable eligibility request; the entries in this array are the ones that had no effect.
Each entry echoes only what the caller sent. The customer's stored installations are never listed.

preview_applied.description:
True when at least one program in this response was evaluated against an APPROVED calculation spec instead of the live ACTIVE one, which only happens on a request that set `include_preview`. Absent or false means every program was evaluated exactly as an ordinary lookup would evaluate it, so the amounts match what a customer sees today.
Read it as a warning, not as a per-program marker: it says the response as a whole contains at least one unpublished evaluation, not which program that was. A preview response carries no accuracy guarantee and must not be stored as a quote.
Report rows carry the same field, because a report row serializes the same result this endpoint returns.

LockedUtilityPrograms.description: Utility programs withheld by a plan restriction. No current plan restricts utility programs, so this field is absent.

program_count.description: How many locked utility programs would pay this customer.

install_amount.description: Sum of the locked programs' incentives paid at install time.

ongoing_amount.description: Sum of the locked programs' recurring incentives, PER YEAR.

device_id.description: The catalog `device.id` the skipped entry named.

partner_device_reference.description: The `partner_device_reference` the caller supplied on this entry, or null when the entry omitted it. Never a server-generated value — nothing was written, so no reference was assigned.

reason.description: `NOT_ON_EXISTING_CUSTOMER`: the request resolved to a customer that already exists, and this entry named an installation that customer does not have.

PartnerBranding.description: Your brand name and logo as configured on your Leap account, so a surface rendering these results can show your branding without a second call.

logo_url.description: URL to your logo, as configured on your Leap account. Null when no logo is configured.

upfront_amount.description: Reserved for a payment kind Leap does not pay yet, so it is always 0. Read `install_amount` for the one-time total.

install_amount.description: Total one-time incentives across all eligible programs, paid at install time.

ongoing_amount.description: Total recurring incentives across all eligible programs, **per year**.

name.description: Program name as shown to the customer. Leap sets this for utility, state, and market programs; for your own partner offer it is the offer name you configure in the portal.

operator_name.description: The utility or agency that operates the program, as shown to the customer. On your own partner offer it is the operator name you configure in the portal. Null when Leap holds no display name for the program.

upfront_amount.description: Reserved for a payment kind Leap does not pay yet, so it is always 0. Read `install_amount` for this program's one-time incentive.

install_amount.description: This program's one-time incentive, paid at install time.

display_name.description: Partner offers only: the branded offer name shown to the customer, as configured in the portal. Null for rebate programs.

logo_url.description: Partner offers only: URL to the logo shown alongside the offer, as configured in the portal. Null for rebate programs.

terms_url.description: Partner offers only: URL to the offer's terms and conditions, as configured in the portal. Null for rebate programs.

description.description: Partner offers only: the offer description shown to the customer, as configured in the portal. Null for rebate programs.

is_partner_offer.description: `true` when this entry is your own partner offer (which bundles one or more underlying programs); `false` for utility, state, and market rebate programs. Use it to separate your offer from rebates in your own UI.

covered_programs.description: Partner offers only: the rebate programs bundled into this offer that the customer qualified for, and whose value is summed into this entry's amounts. Empty for every other kind of entry.

program_identifier.description: Stable identifier for this program — your offer's identifier for a partner offer, or the catalog identifier (for example `PGE-ART`) otherwise. Use it to correlate the same program across lookups.

included_leap_program_ids.description: Partner offers only: identifiers of the underlying programs this offer covers for this customer. Empty for every other kind of entry.

excluded_programs.description: PARTNER_OFFER rows only: the underlying Leap programs that passed both sides of the offer but that stacking left out of it, by name and excluder. They carry no amount, like `covered_programs`: a Leap program's offer-side value is not split out. None of it is in this row's amounts or in `incentive_summary`. Empty for non-offer rows. Absent on results computed before this field shipped, which means unknown, not none.

tiers.description: The program's incentive tiers evaluated for this customer. Each tier carries its payment type, total amount, and per-device results.

tier_id.description: Stable tier identifier: the spec tier id for non-offer programs, or the offer spec's payment-leg tier id for Partner Offer rows. Always present. Prefer `tier_name` for display when it is present; this field is stable across relabeling and safe to use as a join key.

tier_name.description: Customer-facing display name for the tier, when one exists. Non-offer programs surface the spec tier's `label` when the author set one; absent when the tier has no authored label — this field never falls back to `tier_id`. Partner Offer legs always populate this — "Enrollment Incentive" (up-front leg) / "Participation Incentive" (recurring leg). Partner Offers emit one tier per payment leg.

selected.description:
Whether this tier is part of what the program actually pays. A program's tiers are not always additive: a spec can declare two tiers as mutually exclusive alternatives, or make a bonus depend on a base tier that failed, and a program-scope cap can clamp the total. The engine resolves that and pays a SUBSET; every evaluated tier is still reported here so you can see what was considered.
Read this before showing a tier's `incentive_amount` as money the customer will receive. Sum the amounts of the selected tiers and you get the program's `install_amount` / `ongoing_amount`; sum all of them and you can overstate the award. Austin Energy's home EV charger rebate is the canonical case: two mutually exclusive tiers price at $949 and $900, and the program pays $949.
Absent on results computed before this field shipped. Treat absent as "unknown", not as false, and fall back to the per-program amounts.

incentive_amount.description: Tier total across the devices that passed this tier's requirements; per-device outcomes are in `device_results[]`. Units follow `payment_type`: `UPFRONT` and `INSTALL` amounts are one-time, `ONGOING` amounts are per year.

term_months.description: How long an ONGOING tier keeps paying, in months. Omitted when the spec sets no term (the tier pays for as long as the customer stays enrolled) and on INSTALL / UPFRONT tiers.

starts_after_months.description: Months after enrolment before an ONGOING tier's first payment ("$15/kW annual bill credit in years 2-4" is 12, with `term_months` 36). Omitted when the tier pays from the start, and on INSTALL / UPFRONT tiers. `annual_amount` is the first year of payments, so it begins after this offset.

annual_amount.description: What an ONGOING tier pays in its first year of payments, which begins after `starts_after_months` when that is set: the per-interval amount times the payments that fall in the first year (12 monthly, 4 quarterly, 1 annual, fewer when `term_months` is shorter than a year), or the calc method's seasonal annual value. On a Partner Offer's recurring leg it equals `incentive_amount`. Sum it over the selected ONGOING tiers and you get the program's `ongoing_amount`. Omitted on INSTALL / UPFRONT tiers.

device_results.description: One entry per `customer_device` evaluated for this tier. Each shows whether that install passed/failed/ignored the tier's requirements and the per-check details.

TierEstimate.description: How a `storage_performance` tier reached its amount: every assumption with its source, the battery system, the intermediate steps, a yearly schedule and the notes to show at submission. Present only on `storage_performance` tiers; absent on every other calc method. The tier's amount fields keep their meaning.

assumption_set.description: The stored assumption set the values came from, for example `storage_perf_v1`.

assumptions.description: Each assumption key (`soc_at_event_start`, `reserve_fraction`, `participation_factor`, `discharge_efficiency`, `annual_capacity_fade`, `estimate_horizon_years`, `default_system_kw`) with its value and source.

schedule.description: One entry a year over the estimate horizon. Year one is never faded.

term_total_unfaded.description: The same total with no capacity fade, in USD.

source.description: Where the value came from: `spec`, `partner`, `request`, `modelling` or `default`.

EstimateProgram.description: The program's own numbers, as the spec states them.

window_start_hour.description: Local start hour, 0 to 23. Omitted when the profile minimum is read.

reserve_floor.description: A program-stated reserve floor, as a fraction.

commitment_months.description: A one-time tier's enrolment commitment, echoed only.

EstimateSystem.description: The batteries the tier pays on.

fraction_at_window.description: The dispatchable share of nameplate kWh at the window start, net of reserve.

ProgramStackingOutcome.description: This program's inter-program stacking outcome. A program out of the stack, with `excluded_by` set or `reason: lower_value`, keeps its own amounts on this row for display, but is not summed into `incentive_summary`, report contributions, the locked-programs teaser or a filed application. Eligible and conditionally eligible programs both enter stacking resolution, so a stacking exclusion binds a program that is still pending, and a pending program in the stack reads `included: true`. An ineligible program reads `included: false` with `reason: not_eligible`. A program that requires enrollment in another program is ineligible when none of the programs it requires is in the stack, and its device results carry a check with code `PREREQ-001` that says why. The check names a required program only when that program is in the same response, and otherwise says "another program". Absent on results computed before this field shipped.

included.description: True when the program is in the stack the resolver selected.

excluded_by.description: The selected program whose stacking rule rules this one out. Null otherwise.

reason.description: Null when `included`. `excluded_by_rule`: a stacking rule rules it out (see `excluded_by`). `lower_value`: it could join, but a better-scoring combination left it out. `not_eligible`: the program is ineligible, either for this customer or because none of the programs it requires is in the stack.

identifier.description: The Leap program's identifier, for example `ENERGY-ONLY`.

excluded_by.description: The covered program whose stacking rule rules it out, or null when it lost on value alone.

identifier.description: Identifier of the bundled program. Use it to tell the covered programs apart across lookups; it is not a value any other endpoint accepts.

name.description: Human-readable label for the wrapped program (`program.label`).

partner_device_reference.description: Echoes the `partner_device_reference` from the request's `customer_devices[]` entry.

customer_device_id.description: The `customer_device.id` of the installation evaluated in this result.

eligibility_details.description: Per-requirement check results behind this device's tier `status` — one entry per eligibility rule evaluated.

code.description:
Categorical requirement-type code. Says what KIND of requirement this is, not which individual check produced it.

The vocabulary is `UTIL-*` (utility relationship), `EQUIP-*` (equipment identity, rating and condition), `CONT-*` (contractor, permit and inspection), `VEH-*` (vehicle), `CUST-*` (who the customer is and what they live in), `APP-*` (application timing and signatures), `PREREQ-*` (enrollment in another program this one requires) and `MISC`. Prefixes are stable and matchable, so `code.startsWith("EQUIP-")` is a supported way to group.

`APP-002` is defined by the axis "this requires a signature or declaration from the customer", regardless of subject matter — a terms-and-conditions acceptance, a one-rebate-per-address attestation and a trade-ally confirmation are all `APP-002`.

THE SAME CODE CAN APPEAR ON SEVERAL CHECKS IN ONE RESPONSE. Twenty distinct agreement checks all carry `APP-002`, and a program can require more than one of them, so a single card can show several `APP-002` rows that the customer must each act on. Do not treat `code` as a key: group or de-duplicate by it deliberately, and use `requirement` to tell two rows of the same code apart.

`PREREQ-001` marks a program that requires enrollment in another program in the same lookup. `severity` is `met` when the customer qualifies for a required program, `pending` while that program is still pending, and `blocking` when none is available, none qualifies, or none stays in the stack. `expected_values` lists the required programs this response shows, and `actual_value` names the one that satisfies the requirement.

Codes are additive and stable: an existing code is never renumbered or repurposed, and new kinds arrive as new codes. A check whose kind has not been categorised yet reports `MISC`.

source_program_identifier.description: On a partner offer, the program this check came from — your offer's identifier for checks on the offer itself, or the identifier of an underlying program for checks it inherits. Null on rebate programs.

expected_values.description: The values on the far side of the comparison, in the same display spelling as `reason`. Read with `operator`: for `eq`/`in` these are the values the program accepts, for `neq`/`not_in` the values it rejects, and for `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`/`between` the bounds. Casing permutations a spec enumerates are collapsed, so a spec listing `LEVEL_2`, `LEVEL 2` and `level_2` yields one entry. Null on checks that compare nothing, and on `present`/`absent`.

actual_value.description: The customer's value, in the same display spelling as `reason`. Null when the customer has no value on file, and on checks that compare nothing.

operator.description: The comparison applied: `eq`, `neq`, `in`, `not_in`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `between`, `present`, `absent`. Null on checks that compare nothing.

severity.description: What this check means for the application, derived from `status`: `met` (COMPLETED), `pending` (IGNORED — the customer still has to supply or agree to something) or `blocking` (FAILED). Null when the status is not one of those three.

suppliers.description: The retail suppliers the customer buys energy from: a CCA or a Texas retail electric provider. Empty when there is none. When the customer declared a supplier (`supplier_eiaid` on this request, or one stored by an earlier call), it is the only entry, with `source: declared`. Otherwise every CCA whose territory covers the address appears with `source: territory`; an address on the edge of two CCA territories lists both. A supplier never appears in `primary` or `possible_utilities`.

primary.description: The utility resolved as serving this address — the one whose programs drive the eligibility result.

possible_utilities.description: Every utility whose service territory covers this address (including `primary`); more than one can appear where territories overlap. Only delivery utilities appear here and in `primary`, never a CCA or an agency.

SupplierUtility.description: A retail supplier related to the customer, by EIA id, and how it was found.

eiaid.description: EIA utility identifier of the supplier.

source.description: `declared` when the caller sent it as `supplier_eiaid`, on this request or an earlier one. `territory` when the supplier's territory covers the customer's address.

IncentiveUtility.description: EIA-keyed utility identity used in incentive eligibility responses. Distinct from `common-schemas.yaml#/components/schemas/Utility`, which carries Connect's UUID-based shape with logo + connection URL.

Geocoding.description: The point the lookup evaluated. On Free plans (anything but Business) and ZIP-only requests the coordinates are the ZIP code's centroid, not the street, and `formatted_address` echoes the address as sent.

latitude.description: Latitude of the geocoded address, in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Longitude of the geocoded address, in decimal degrees.

formatted_address.description: The address as normalized by the geocoder.

CustomerClassification.description: The customer or site classification used to determine eligibility. `RESIDENTIAL` and `COMMERCIAL` are the long-standing values; `MULTIFAMILY` and `MANUFACTURED_HOME` exist because rebate qualification differs across single-family, multifamily, and manufactured housing.

IncentivePaymentInterval.description: How often an ONGOING tier pays. Present on ONGOING tiers only; omitted on INSTALL tiers, which pay once.

BearerAuth.description: Your Leap API key as a Bearer token. Send it in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`.
